questions.question: What are the two parts of the oral English exam?
options: A prepared presentation and a follow-up conversation
A written test and a listening test
A grammar quiz and a translation task
A group debate and a written summary
questions.explanation: The oral exam consists of a presentation (about 10 minutes) followed by a conversation with the examiners (about 15-20 minutes).

questions.question: Which of these is one of the things the examiner assesses in the oral exam?
options: Fluency — whether you speak coherently without too many pauses
Your handwriting
How fast you can read aloud
How many quotes you have memorised
questions.explanation: Examiners assess communication, language, content, fluency and interaction — not handwriting or memorisation.

questions.question: Which word contains the voiceless "th" sound /θ/?
options: think
this
weather
that
questions.explanation: "Think" has the voiceless /θ/. "This", "that" and "weather" all have the voiced /ð/ sound.

questions.question: What is a typical Norwegian pronunciation error with the "th" sounds?
options: Replacing them with "d" or "t", saying "da" instead of "the"
Pronouncing them too strongly
Adding an extra vowel before them
Replacing them with "s" in every word
questions.explanation: Norwegian speakers often replace the th-sounds with "d" or "t" ("da" for "the", "tink" for "think") because Norwegian lacks these sounds.

questions.question: How do you pronounce the "w" in words like "water" and "world"?
options: With rounded lips
With the teeth against the lower lip
Exactly like the Norwegian "v"
It is silent
questions.explanation: "W" is made with rounded lips, while "v" is made with the teeth against the lower lip — a contrast many Norwegians mix up.
